document.channel: Consulate of the main destination country

notes: The rules come from the European Commission's own photograph guidelines (DG Migration and Home Affairs), which apply ICAO Doc 9303 to Schengen visa applications.

The Commission states the head as a PERCENTAGE - 'your face takes up 70-80% of the photograph' - not in millimetres, which is why this spec uses passFraction. Reading only passMM used to skip the head check entirely for a spec like this; fixed, and pinned by a test.

The Commission states a width of 35-40 mm and gives no height. 35 x 45 mm is the ICAO size every Schengen consulate accepts, so it is used here; a 40 mm wide photo is also legal but is not what this app produces.

Background: the Commission says 'plain light-coloured', NOT white. A neutral light grey is the ICAO recommendation and separates dark hair from the backdrop better than pure white. This is a choice within the stated rule, not a published value.

Glasses ARE permitted, unlike the US and India, provided the eyes are clearly visible with no flash reflection, no tinted lenses and frames not covering the eyes. The app does not detect glasses, so this is shown to the user rather than enforced.
No EU-wide digital pixel or file size standard exists; individual consulates and VFS centres set their own. The range here is 35 x 45 mm at 300 to 600 dpi.
Lighting and sharpness thresholds are this app's own calibration, shared with the other specs. The Commission requires uniform lighting with no shadows or flash reflections but states no numbers.

headHeight.note: The Commission states 70-80% of the photograph. On a 45 mm photo that is 31.5-36.0 mm. The target is 75%, the middle of the band.

background.editingRisk: We replaced the background with a neutral light grey. Consulates differ on edited backgrounds, so a photo taken against a plain light wall is safer.

sources.title: European Commission, DG Migration and Home Affairs: ICAO photograph guidelines
sources.says: no more than 6 months old; 35-40 mm in width; close up of head and top of shoulders so that your face takes up 70-80% of the photograph; in sharp focus and clear; plain light-coloured background; uniform lighting with no shadows or flash reflections and no red eye; eyes open and clearly visible; facing square on, not tilted; neutral expression and mouth closed; shown alone; glasses permitted if eyes are clear, with no flash reflection, no tinted lenses and frames not covering the eyes; head coverings only for religious reasons

sources.title: European Commission: Applying for a Schengen visa
sources.says: A photo in compliance with ICAO standards is required with a Schengen visa application
